title: Redwood security review - SSO / SCIM / RBAC - MedFin Health
summary: High-level security review focused on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC design. Customer requires SOC 2 + ISO references, audit log detail, KMS support, and confirmation of least-privilege roles. Agreed next steps: share security pack, sample SAML metadata, SCIM test plan, and a proposed RBAC mapping for their org. Plan follow-up POC for SCIM-enabled provisioning and role testing.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. We'll do a high level security review and dive into SSO / SCIM and RBAC. Priya, Samir are here from the engineering side.
00:12 Carlos Mendes: Thanks, Jordan. From MedFin we have Leah on security, Anita who owns identity, and Tom on platform. We got your calendar invite, and the goal is to validate the SAML flow and provisioning model before we start a pilot. Also need to confirm audit log retention and KMS support for PII.
00:30 Priya Rao: Great. Quick agenda — we will run through our SAML capabilities, SCIM for user/group provisioning, RBAC patterns and least-privilege recommendations, then cover logging, encryption/KMS, and data residency. We'll leave 10 mins at the end for questions.
00:45 Leah Park: Sounds good. Two quick constraints — our IdP is Okta (enterprise) and we have SCIM automated through an internal tooling layer; we prefer SCIM push but can also support just SAML for now. Also we need audit logs to be exportable to our SIEM for 365 days.
01:02 Samir Patel: Okay thanks. On SAML, Redwood supports SAML 2.0 — metadata exchange, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. We also support Just-in-Time provisioning if you prefer not to use SCIM. There are a couple of fields we map by default (email, first/last name, groups).
01:23 Anita Rao: Does Redwood support SCIM 2.0 with group push? We need group memberships to control access to projects — that's critical for least-privilege.
01:35 Priya Rao: Yes, we support SCIM 2.0 full user and group push, including incremental patch operations. Small note — in some older exports the group attribute name can be different, so we have a config parameter for mapping group identifiers.
01:50 Tom Wu: For RBAC, how granular are roles? We need a model that can map to our internal roles: viewer, editor, admin, and a separate role for billing ops. Can Redwood do custom roles per workspace and also restrict model access by role?
02:08 Samir Patel: We recommend a least-privilege model that uses three base role templates (viewer/editor/admin) plus attribute-based overrides for billing and SRE functions. You can scope roles to routes, model families, or environments (prod/staging). Role application is enforced at the API key/token level and in the Console.
02:26 Leah Park: Is RBAC integrated with SCIM groups so we can keep role assignments centralized in Okta?
02:34 Priya Rao: Yes, mapping SCIM groups to Redwood roles is standard. When SCIM pushes a group, you can define an automatic role mapping. We also support provisioning to multiple teams/tenants if you need multi-tenant separation.
02:50 Carlos Mendes: On encryption — our policy mandates customer-managed keys (CMK) for production. Do you support KMS integration and HSM-backed keys?
03:02 Samir Patel: For Private deployments we support KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys; for Dedicated/Hosted we offer KMS integration via standard providers (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS) and can do Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for enterprise plans. HSM is available via dedicated contracts.
03:20 Leah Park: We need to ensure logs of who accessed which model and which prompts were run are retained. What level of audit logging do you capture?
03:32 Priya Rao: We capture token-level request metadata — caller, route, model variant, timestamp, latency, and status codes. By default we do not store full customer prompt content in longer-term logs unless you enable it; we can support logging prompts in secure, encrypted logs if needed for debugging under an agreement. We also export logs to customer-owned S3 (or GCP bucket) via a secure pipeline for retention.
03:58 Anita Rao: How about compliance artifacts — SOC 2 and ISO? We need evidence for our audit — is your attestation current?
04:08 Jordan Blake: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and has ISO 27001 — we will share the latest attestations and the security pack. I'll attach the certs and the control mapping for Okta/SCIM in the follow-up.
04:22 Carlos Mendes: Good. A few technical nitpicks — our IdP uses SAML with SHA256 signing and encrypted assertions. Any caveats?
04:34 Priya Rao: That's fine. We support SHA256, encrypted assertions, and signed metadata. For SP metadata we publish a standard URL; for IdP metadata you'd upload it via the Console or send it to us. We also support metadata signed by the IdP.
04:51 Tom Wu: For SCIM test plan — we want to run a test where we create a user, add them to a group, see provisioning, then remove and confirm deprovisioning within 5 minutes. Is that feasible?
05:03 Samir Patel: Absolutely. Typical SCIM cycles are near real-time; depends on your IdP sync window, but patch and delete operations are immediate on push. We can provide a test harness and a sandbox tenant for MedFin.
05:18 Leah Park: About least-privilege — can we do time-bound elevated access? E.g., temp admin for SRE for 1 hour.
05:29 Priya Rao: We have temporary role elevation workflows integrated with SSO sessions and can integrate with your identity governance tool for time-bound access. If you want to use a manual approval flow, that's configurable too.
05:42 Carlos Mendes: Data residency — our regs require data at rest for EU accounts to stay in EU regions. We have EU users and also a US tenant. Does Redwood isolate data by region?
05:55 Samir Patel: Yes — for Hosted we can pin tenant data regionally; for Dedicated/Private you can deploy in your VPC region. We support per-tenant regional pinning and also network isolation for the private offering.
06:12 Anita Rao: Audit log export — can those go to our Splunk? We want logs in a format Splunk can ingest and with a guaranteed delivery SLA.
06:22 Priya Rao: We support log export to S3/GCS and direct streaming to Splunk via a forwarder. Delivery SLA for exports is part of the enterprise contract; we'll share the options.
06:34 Leah Park: A common failure mode is orphaned admin accounts after contractors leave. How does Redwood handle deprovisioned users — do API keys get revoked automatically when SCIM deletes a user?
06:48 Samir Patel: If SCIM deprovisions a user we can automatically revoke associated tokens and API keys or shadow them and require a manual review — policy is configurable. We recommend automatic revocation for security-sensitive orgs.
07:02 Carlos Mendes: Great. A couple of questions from procurement — do you offer customer-managed logging retention policies? Also any PII minimization defaults?
07:14 Jordan Blake: Yes — retention windows are configurable per-export and per-tenant. By default we minimize PII in logs; prompts and responses are not stored in standard logs unless you opt in. For PII-heavy workflows we recommend private deployment or using BYOK and strict retention.
07:33 Tom Wu: On SAML metadata exchange — do you have an IdP metadata upload API? We automate onboarding via Terraform.
07:42 Priya Rao: We have APIs for programmatic SAML/SCIM setup and Terraform providers for Dedicated/Private customers. For Hosted we also support automation via our onboarding API. We'll send the API docs and a sample Terraform snippet.
07:58 Anita Rao: Any gotchas with SCIM group-to-role mapping and nested groups? We have nested groups in Okta.
08:08 Samir Patel: We flatten nested groups during sync but preserve the membership semantics; there are config knobs to control flattening depth. Nested group mapping is supported but we document performance implications for extremely large group graphs.
08:26 Leah Park: Regarding encryption keys — if we use AWS KMS CMK, what is the process for key rotation and who has access to the plaintext keys?
08:36 Priya Rao: With BYOK, you control the KMS and key rotation. Redwood requests decryption via KMS APIs for runtime operations; we never persist plaintext keys. Access is audited and restricted to runtime nodes; key usage is logged in both your KMS and our audit trails.
08:58 Carlos Mendes: For the POC we want SCIM provisioning + RBAC role mapping to be tested. What would you need from us to provision the sandbox?
09:08 Jordan Blake: We'll need an Okta service account with SCIM permissions (OAuth token or basic auth depending on your setup), SAML metadata, and a list of groups and the desired role mappings. Priya will share a template for the mapping.
09:22 Priya Rao: I'll share the SCIM mapping template and a sample postman collection for test flows. We'll also set up a sandbox org and coordinate a day for the provisioning test.
09:35 Tom Wu: On logs again — can we redact prompt content before exporting? We have legal constraints.
09:44 Priya Rao: Yes, we have a server-side redaction pipeline that can remove or hash prompt content prior to export. That can be run as a default transform on export buckets.
09:55 Anita Rao: Ok, last question — do you support SAML attribute-based access control? We want to pass department attributes for ABAC.
10:05 Samir Patel: We support ABAC via attributes from SAML assertions or SCIM profile attributes; you can reference attributes in role rules.
10:15 Jordan Blake: Wrap-up — we will: 1) share SOC2/ISO certs and security pack, 2) send SCIM mapping template and SAML metadata instructions, 3) provision sandbox for SCIM tests, 4) propose RBAC mapping doc for your review.
10:28 Carlos Mendes: Cool. Timeline — we'd like to start the POC next week if possible. Procurement signoff pending but security gating is the blocker.
10:40 Jordan Blake: Understood. We'll aim to have docs and sandbox ready within 48 hours. Priya, Samir — can you own the technical setup?
10:49 Priya Rao: Yep, we'll own the setup and run the test plan.
10:53 Samir Patel: I'll coordinate with Tom on the sandbox network and SCIM credentials.
10:58 Leah Park: Thanks everyone. We'll look for the security pack and mapping template.
11:05 Jordan Blake: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the provisioning test.
11:12 <<call ends>>
